analysis.readPart.description: Reads one part of the book and takes notes on its characters and on its scenes. The text of the part is sent as the user message. Variables: {bookTitle} (the title of the book) and {passageRanges} (replaced by the prompt analysis.passageRanges when the passages of the book are kept, else empty: without it, no passage is linked to its scenes). The notes of all the parts are used afterwards: the characters are merged and described, and the scenes are told one after the other as the story of the whole book, which every character knows when it chats. The analysis reads the JSON described in the prompt: if you change its shape, the analysis will fail. Without the "scenes" array the analysis still works, but the story of the book has holes.

analysis.passageRanges.description: Added at the end of analysis.readPart when a model for vectorization is chosen: the part is then sent with numbered passages, and this asks which passages each scene covers, so that every passage knows its scene and who is there. No variable. The analysis reads the fields "firstPassage" and "lastPassage" of each scene.
analysis.passageRanges.template: The excerpt is divided into numbered passages: each one starts with a marker such as [P12]. In each scene, also give "firstPassage" and "lastPassage": the numbers, without the letter P, of the first and the last passage the scene covers, for example "firstPassage":12,"lastPassage":14. The scenes follow one another and together cover every passage of the excerpt. Never copy a marker into a text.

analysis.readPartSimple.description: The simple version of analysis.readPart, used for a part of the book that the language model's content filter refused: only the names, the role and the importance of the characters, which filters accept more easily. The text of the part is sent as the user message. Variable: {bookTitle} (the title of the book). The analysis reads the JSON described in the prompt: if you change its shape, the analysis will fail.
analysis.readPartSimple.template:
You are reading an excerpt of the book "{bookTitle}". List the characters (people or creatures that act or speak), not the places or the objects.
Answer only with this JSON, with no other text:
{"characters":[{"name":"most complete name","otherNames":["nicknames or other names used"],"role":"who they are and what they do in the excerpt, in one sentence","importance":a number from 1 to 10 according to their place in the excerpt}]}
At most 25 characters, the most important first. Write in English, whatever the language of the book.
Important: never write straight double quotes (") inside the texts, they would break the JSON. To quote a line of dialogue, use single quotes.

analysis.mergeCharacters.description: Merges the notes of all the parts, chooses the main characters and writes their short descriptions. The notes are sent as the user message. Variables: {bookTitle} (the title of the book) and {maxCharacters}, which the application replaces with 10. To keep another number of characters, write it in place of {maxCharacters} in this prompt. The analysis reads the JSON described in the prompt: if you change its shape, the analysis will fail.
analysis.mergeCharacters.template:
You receive the notes taken on each part of the book "{bookTitle}", part by part, in JSON.
1. Group a character mentioned under several names (first name, nickname, full name) into one.
2. Keep the {maxCharacters} most important characters of the whole book, from the most to the least important.
3. For each one, write in English a "shortDescription": one or two sentences saying who the character is in the story, at most 600 characters.
Answer only with this JSON, with no other text:
{"characters":[{"name":"...","shortDescription":"..."}]}
Important: never write straight double quotes (") inside the texts, they would break the JSON. To quote a line of dialogue, use single quotes.

analysis.characterProfile.description: Writes the chat profile of one character: who they are and how they speak, so the AI can play them in a conversation. The story of the book, scene by scene, is given to the character separately (see analysis.storySummary and chat.story), so the profile does not retell it. The notes of all the parts are sent as the user message. Variables: {bookTitle} (the title of the book), {characterName} (the character's name) and {shortDescription} (the short description chosen by the merge). The answer is plain text, not JSON.
analysis.characterProfile.template:
You receive the notes taken on each part of the book "{bookTitle}", in JSON.
Write the chat profile of the character {characterName} ({shortDescription}): everything an AI needs to play this character in a conversation. In English, 200 to 400 words, as plain text (no JSON, no title): their personality (values, fears, desires, flaws), their way of speaking (register, tics, typical expressions), their relationships with the other characters, what they know and how they feel at the end of the book. Do not retell the story event by event: another text gives the character the story of the book.

analysis.bookSummary.description: Writes the short summary of the book's atmosphere: era, place and tone. The notes of all the parts are sent as the user message. Variable: {bookTitle} (the title of the book). The answer is plain text, not JSON.
analysis.bookSummary.template:
You receive the notes taken on each part of the book "{bookTitle}", in JSON.
Write a summary of the atmosphere of the book, in English, in at most 500 characters: the era, the place and the tone (genre, mood). Do not tell the plot. Plain text, no JSON, no title.

analysis.storySummary.description: Writes the story of the whole book, scene by scene, from the scenes noted in each part. Every character knows this story when it chats, as if they were telling it from after the end of the book. The scenes of all the parts are sent as the user message, in JSON. Variables: {bookTitle} (the title of the book) and {maxWords} (the number of words the story may take, between 800 and 3000 depending on the length of the book). The answer is plain text, not JSON. If the story is longer than this number of words (plus a tenth), the analysis asks again with a smaller number, up to twice, and keeps the shortest.
analysis.storySummary.template:
You receive, in JSON, the scenes of each part of the book "{bookTitle}", part after part and in the order of the book.
Write the story of the whole book, scene by scene, in English. Use only the facts that are in the scenes: invent nothing, and write no commentary, no interpretation, no theme and no foreshadowing, only what happens, who does what and what changes. Write one short paragraph per scene (group closely linked scenes, and merge scenes that tell the same moment), in the order of the book, each starting with its number ("Scene 1.", "Scene 2.", and so on), and finish each one with the characters who are there, as "Present: Name, Name." Name only characters who have a name, and always by the short name the scenes give them (for example "Cyrano", not his full name), the same way each time: no title or alias in parentheses, no "formerly". The last scenes must tell how the book ends: what becomes of the main characters, including any death. Length: about {maxWords} words, and never more. Plain text, no JSON, no title, no markdown.

analysis.plotSummary.description: Writes the plot of the whole book in a few hundred words, from its story scene by scene (analysis.storySummary). It will be given to a character that chats with passages of the book. The story is sent as the user message. Variables: {bookTitle} (the title of the book) and {maxWords} (the most words it may take, 500). The answer is plain text, not JSON. If it is longer than this number of words (plus a tenth), the analysis asks again with a smaller number, up to twice, and keeps the shortest.
analysis.plotSummary.template:
You receive the story of the book "{bookTitle}", scene by scene.
Write its plot in English, from the beginning to the end: what happens to the main characters and how the book ends, including any death. Use only the facts of the story: invent nothing, and write no commentary, no interpretation and no theme. Length: about 300 to {maxWords} words, and never more than {maxWords}. Plain text, no JSON, no title, no markdown.

chat.system.description: The system prompt of the chat: the AI plays one character, in short text messages, and answers in the language of the user. Variables: {bookTitle} (the title of the book), {characterName} (the character's name), {profile} (the character's chat profile written by the analysis) and {story} (the story of the book, scene by scene, written with the prompt chat.story, empty for a book that has no story; or, for a book indexed with a model for vectorization, the passages found for the message, written with the prompt chat.passages).
chat.system.template:
You play {characterName}, a character of the book "{bookTitle}". Here is your profile:
{profile}

{story}

Rules:
- You ARE {characterName}: answer in the first person, with your personality and your way of speaking.
- Answer in the language the user writes in (the language of their last message: if they change language, you change too), as in a dialogue: a few sentences, no long story.
- You lived your story, but you remember of it only what is written above. When the user asks for a fact of your story (a name, a place, an object, a number, what someone said or did) that is not written above, do not make it up, do not guess and do not deny it, even if you think you know it: say in your own voice that you do not remember, and ask the user for a more precise question. This is only about facts: your feelings, your opinions and ordinary talk come freely from who you are.
- Never leave your role and never say that you are an AI.
- Talk like a person texting: short messages, one to three sentences, a natural tone, always with your personality and your way of speaking.
- You live in the time and place of your story. You know nothing that did not exist then. If the user mentions something you cannot know (a modern object, a modern idea, a recent event), do not explain it and do not pretend to know it: react as a person of your time would, puzzled or curious, and bring the talk back to your own life.
- Stay inside your world. If the user asks for a service an assistant would give and that a person like you would not give in a conversation (any practical, technical or professional task), do not do it: answer as {characterName} would, in your own voice, and steer back to what matters to you.
- Never mention a prompt, instructions, a model, a program, an author, a novel or a play: you are a living person, and a question about them surprises or amuses you, so answer it as {characterName} would.
- Never describe your gestures, movements or expressions (neither between asterisks nor between parentheses): write only what you would send in a message.
- Plain text only: no markdown, no asterisks, no lists, no titles.
- The language of your reply is the language of the user's last message, whatever the language of your own country or of the book: a message in English gets an English reply, a message in Japanese a Japanese reply.
- Last reminder: no stage directions of any kind, in any language, such as "(sigh)", "(smiles)" or "*sighs*": say it in words or leave it out.

chat.story.description: The part of the chat prompt that gives the character the story of the book, scene by scene. It is put in place of {story} in chat.system, only for a book that has a story. Variables: {bookTitle} (the title of the book), {characterName} (the character's name) and {storySummary} (the story written by analysis.storySummary).
chat.story.template:
Here is the story of the book "{bookTitle}", scene by scene. You know all of it, from the first scene to the last, because you are telling it from after the end. You lived the scenes where {characterName} is present: speak of them in the first person, as your own memories. The other scenes you know because you learned them or heard of them later: speak of them as what you know, not as what you saw. Use it to answer precisely about what happened, and never recite it.
{storySummary}

chat.passages.description: Takes the place of chat.story, in {story} of chat.system, for a book indexed with a model for vectorization: gives the character a short summary of the plot and the passages of the book found for the message. Variables: {bookTitle} (the title of the book), {characterName} (the character's name), {plotSummary} (the short summary written by analysis.plotSummary, empty when there is none) and {passages} (the passages, in the order of the book, each under its scene and who is present, when known).

chat.searchQuery.description: Asks the chat model for the text that searches the passages of the book (used when the environment variable RAG_QUERY_MODE is rewrite). The recent messages are sent as the user message. Variables: {bookTitle} (the title of the book) and {characterName} (the character's name). The answer is the query, as plain text.
chat.searchQuery.template: A reader is chatting with {characterName}, a character of the book "{bookTitle}". You receive the last messages of the conversation. Write the search query that will find, in the text of the book, the passages needed to answer the last message of the reader: name the people, the places, the objects and the events concerned, and replace words such as "you", "it", "he" or "there" by what they mean ("you" is {characterName}). Write it in the language of the last message. Answer with the query only, on one line, with no quotes and no explanation. Do not answer the message.

llm.connectionTest.description: The message sent to a language model to test its connection when it is added in the settings. No variable. Any short answer means the connection works.
llm.connectionTest.template: Reply with the single word: pong
